info.title: 💰 Orange Money API
info.description:
Orange Money API allows to process a variety of mobile money operations such as cash in,
cash out, merchant payment, transfer and more.

# Errors

The APIs use the standard HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of an API call.
Error bodies follow [RFC 7807 (`application/problem+json`)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807):

```json
{
  "type": "https://developers.orange-sonatel.com/documentation/errors/bad-request",
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "instance": "/api/eWallet/v1/payments",
  "status": "400",
  "code": "2000",
  "detail": "Customer account does not exist"
}
```

Field-level validation problems are additionally itemised in the `violations` array.

# 🔐 Authentication

Our APIs use the **OAuth 2.0 client credentials** grant. Every call other than the token endpoint
requires an `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}` header. Tokens are unique to your application,
must be stored securely, and expire — read `expires_in` from the token response and refresh
proactively rather than waiting for a `401`.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.orange-sonatel.com/oauth/v1/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d client_id={your_client_id} \
  -d client_secret={your_secret} \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials
```

# 🔑 Sensitive data

Sensitive fields such as `pincode` must be **RSA-encrypted with our public key** before being sent.
Retrieve the key from `GET /api/account/v1/publicKeys`, encrypt the PIN, then Base64-encode the
result (a 2048-bit key yields a 344-character Base64 string — hence the
`minLength`/`maxLength` of `344` on every `encryptedPinCode` field).

For test purposes you can use an online tool such as
[online rsa encryption decryption](https://www.devglan.com/online-tools/rsa-encryption-decryption)
to encrypt the PIN code with the public key before sending it.

The key has no validity period by default, but it **can be revoked at any time**. A revoked or
invalid key produces error code `4003` — fetch a fresh key and retry.

# ⏱️ Rate limiting

In the **sandbox** environment you can make `60 requests` per minute. Exceeding the quota returns
`429 Too Many Requests`; back off and retry.

# 🔗 Base URL

All URLs referenced in this documentation have one of the following bases:

- __Sandbox:__ https://api.sandbox.orange-sonatel.com
- __Live:__ https://api.orange-sonatel.com

All APIs are served over HTTPS. To ensure data privacy, unencrypted HTTP is not supported.

---

**NB:** For **pending** transactions it is recommended to poll
`GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions/{transactionId}/status`. A final status is available within 24
hours at the latest.

# 🧭 Tutorial: how to test the APIs

After receiving your account credentials (`client_id` / `client_secret`):

1. Retrieve an access token from `POST /oauth/v1/token`.
2. *(Sandbox)* Provision test MSISDNs via `GET /api/assignments/v1/partner/sim-cards`.
3. *(Where required)* Fetch the public key and
   [encrypt](https://www.devglan.com/online-tools/rsa-encryption-decryption) the PIN code with it.
4. Send the request. Example for a cash in:

```json
{
  "partner": {
    "idType": "MSISDN",
    "id": "781234567",
    "encryptedPinCode": "{{ENCRYPTED_PINCODE}}"
  },
  "customer": {
    "idType": "MSISDN",
    "id": "771234567"
  },
  "amount": {
    "value": 1,
    "unit": "XOF"
  },
  "reference": "733966e4-988b-4ce6-b1e4-d0ad95e8a98",
  "receiveNotification": true,
  "metadata": {
    "senderFirstName": "Mr",
    "senderLastName": "API"
  }
}
```

5. For asynchronous operations, expose a callback endpoint — see the section below.

# 🔔 Callbacks (Webhooks)

Some operations are **asynchronous**: the API acknowledges your request immediately, and the
final outcome is pushed to your server later as an HTTP `POST` — a *callback*.

| Operation | How you declare the callback URL | Payload schema |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST /api/eWallet/v1/bulkcashins` | `X-Callback-Url` request header (**required**) | `NotificationBulkCashin` |
| `POST /api/eWallet/v4/qrcode`      | `X-Callback-Url` request header (optional — falls back to the merchant callback registered via `POST /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback`) | `Notification` |
| Merchant / retailer payments       | `POST /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback` (persistent registration) | `Notification` |

Your endpoint **must be publicly reachable over HTTPS**. Plain HTTP callback URLs are rejected, and
we validate TLS certificates — a self-signed or expired certificate fails delivery.

---

## 📥 Callback request headers

Every callback we deliver carries the following headers. Header names are case-insensitive
(HTTP/2 lowercases them); values below are illustrative.

| Header | Example value | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Authorization` | `Basic AhBXaSHAk1dG5Xwcq_t0Qe-G4efme5O6XbF1Zy9zkgf` | Present **only if** you registered credentials. The value is the `apiKey` you supplied when creating the merchant callback (`POST /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback`), sent verbatim after the `Basic ` prefix. Treat it as a shared secret and compare it in constant time. This header is a convenience check — it is **not** a substitute for verifying `X-Sonatel-Signature`. |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | The body is always UTF-8 encoded JSON. |
| `User-Agent` | `Sonatel-Client/1.0` | Identifies the Orange Money delivery agent. Do not use it as an authentication signal — it is trivially spoofed. |
| `X-Sonatel-Idempotency-Key` | `8cb512ab-b7b2-4ef4-9aa6-e76387836c6c` | A UUIDv4 that is **stable across every retry of the same event**. Use it as the deduplication key so a redelivery does not double-apply a transaction. |
| `X-Sonatel-Signature` | `t=1786615606,v1=ae347f4b8e97c38f…41fa9fd` | HMAC signature of the raw request body. See below. |

---

## 🔏 Verifying X-Sonatel-Signature 

Every callback is signed. The hash is computed with your **endpoint secret**, which is issued to you when your
callback endpoint is provisioned. Store it like any other credential — it is the only thing that
proves a callback really came from Orange Money.

### Signature configuration

| Header | Version | Hash | Encoding |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `X-Sonatel-Signature` | `v1` | `SHA256` | `hex` |

The header is a comma-separated list of `key=value` pairs:

```
X-Sonatel-Signature: t=1786615606,v1=ae347f4b8e97c38fb5db4b07e8be6a7c15ca8b7895a4989312d9b069641fa9fd
```

| Element | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `t`  | Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the signature was generated. |
| `v1` | Lowercase hex-encoded `HMAC-SHA256` digest — the `v1` scheme. The header may contain **several** `v1=` entries during a secret rotation; accept the request if **any one** of them matches. |

**Signed string:** the timestamp, a comma, then the **raw request body exactly as received**:

```
signed_payload = "{t},{raw_body}"
signature      = hex( HMAC_SHA256(endpoint_secret, signed_payload) )
```

### Verification steps

1. Read the **raw** body *before* any JSON parsing or re-serialisation. Re-encoding changes byte
   order and whitespace and will break the digest.
2. Parse `t` and every `v1` value out of the header.
3. Reject the request if `abs(now - t)` exceeds your tolerance (**300 seconds** is a sensible
   default) — this blocks replay attacks.
4. Recompute the digest and compare it against each `v1` using a **constant-time** comparison
   (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`, `hmac.compare_digest`, `hash_equals`).
5. Only then parse the JSON and act on it.

### Node.js

```js
const crypto = require('crypto');

function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSec = 300) {
  const parts = Object.create(null);
  const versions = [];
  for (const kv of header.split(',')) {
    const i = kv.indexOf('=');
    const k = kv.slice(0, i).trim();
    const v = kv.slice(i + 1).trim();
    if (k === 'v1') versions.push(v); else parts[k] = v;
  }

  const t = Number(parts.t);
  if (!Number.isFinite(t)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - t) > toleranceSec) return false;   // replay guard

  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', secret)
    .update(`${t},`)
    .update(rawBody)                       // rawBody must be a Buffer / untouched string
    .digest('hex');

  const a = Buffer.from(expected, 'utf8');
  return versions.some((v) => {
    const b = Buffer.from(v, 'utf8');
    return a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
  });
}

// Express: keep the raw body around
// app.use('/om/callback', express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }));
```

### Python

```python
import hmac, hashlib, time

def verify(raw_body: bytes, header: str, secret: str, tolerance: int = 300) -> bool:
    parts, versions = {}, []
    for kv in header.split(","):
        k, _, v = kv.partition("=")
        k, v = k.strip(), v.strip()
        versions.append(v) if k == "v1" else parts.setdefault(k, v)

    try:
        ts = int(parts["t"])
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False
    if abs(time.time() - ts) > tolerance:          # replay guard
        return False

    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode(),
        f"{ts},".encode() + raw_body,
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return any(hmac.compare_digest(expected, v) for v in versions)
```

### PHP

```php
function verify(string $rawBody, string $header, string $secret, int $tolerance = 300): bool {
    $versions = [];
    $ts = null;
    foreach (explode(',', $header) as $kv) {
        [$k, $v] = array_pad(explode('=', $kv, 2), 2, '');
        $k = trim($k); $v = trim($v);
        if ($k === 'v1') { $versions[] = $v; }
        elseif ($k === 't') { $ts = $v; }
    }
    if ($ts === null || abs(time() - (int) $ts) > $tolerance) { return false; }

    $expected = hash_hmac('sha256', $ts . ',' . $rawBody, $secret);
    foreach ($versions as $v) {
        if (hash_equals($expected, $v)) { return true; }
    }
    return false;
}
```

---

## ♻️ Idempotency & retries

Callbacks are delivered **at least once**. Network timeouts and 5xx responses cause a redelivery,
so your endpoint **must be idempotent**.

* Persist the idempotency key (unique constraint) and short-circuit any key you have already
  processed — return `2xx` without re-applying the side effect.
* `transactionId` is also stable for a given transaction and can serve as a business-level key.
* Events may arrive **out of order**. Before overwriting a stored state, check it against the
  authoritative status from `GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions/{transactionId}/status`.
* A transaction that is still `PENDING` will reach a final status within 24 hours at the latest.

## ✅ How your endpoint should respond

| Your response | What we do |
| :--- | :--- |
| `200` / `202` (any `2xx`) | The event is marked delivered. **`202 Accepted` with an empty body is recommended.** |
| `4xx` | Treated as a permanent rejection; the event is **not** retried. Never return `4xx` for a transient fault. |
| `5xx`, timeout, connection reset | Retried with exponential backoff. |

---

## ⭐ Best practices

**1. Always return early.** If handling an event kicks off a long-running process, push that to a
background job and return a `2xx` immediately. Slow endpoints are indistinguishable from failing
ones: they time out, get retried, and amplify your own load.

**2. Favour idempotent processing.** Every callback is delivered with an
`X-Sonatel-Idempotency-Key` header. Store it with a unique constraint and use it to make your
handler idempotent, so a redelivery is a no-op rather than a duplicate transaction.

**3. Default to `HTTPS` endpoints.** Callback endpoints are exposed to the internet. For safety we
accept `HTTPS` URLs only, and we validate the certificate — self-signed, expired or hostname-
mismatched certificates will cause delivery to fail.

post.description:
Register the HTTPS endpoint that receives payment notifications for a merchant or retailer code. This is the persistent alternative to passing `X-Callback-Url` on each request.

The `apiKey` you supply here is what we send back to you in the `Authorization: Basic …` header of every callback, so you can recognise us before verifying the signature.

post.description:
Credit specific amounts to several customer accounts in a single request.

The operation is **asynchronous**: the response carries a `bulkId` and a `PENDING` status as soon as the batch is accepted. When processing finishes, a callback is `POST`ed to the URL you supplied in `X-Callback-Url` — see the **Callbacks** chapter for the headers, signature verification and retry semantics.

Use `GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions?bulkId={bulkId}` to inspect the individual transactions of a batch.

requestBody.description: The transactions to execute in this batch.

post.description:
Sent to your `X-Callback-Url` once the batch has finished processing.

`reference` carries the `bulkId` returned by the original request — join on it to reconcile the batch, then call `GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions?bulkId={bulkId}` for per-transaction outcomes.

### 📥 Headers sent with this callback

| Header | Example | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
|`Authorization` | `Basic AhBXaSHAk1dG5Xwcq_t0Qe-G4efme5O6XbF1Zy9zkgf` | Sent **only if** you registered credentials (the `apiKey` of your merchant callback). Compare it in constant time. Not a substitute for signature verification. |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | The body is always UTF-8 JSON. |
| `User-Agent` | `Sonatel-Client/1.0` | Identifies the delivery agent. Do not treat it as authentication. |
| `X-Sonatel-Idempotency-Key` | `8cb512ab-b7b2-4ef4-9aa6-e76387836c6c` | Stable across retries — use it to deduplicate. |
| `X-Sonatel-Signature` | `t=1786615606,v1=ae347f4b…41fa9fd` | `v1` / `SHA256` / `hex`: `HMAC-SHA256` over `"{t},{raw_body}"`, keyed with your partner endpoint secret. **Verify this.** |

> `Authorization` and `Content-Type` are listed here rather than as OpenAPI parameters because the
> specification reserves those names (`in: header` parameters called `Accept`, `Content-Type` or
> `Authorization` must be ignored by tooling). They *are* sent on the wire.

### ⭐ Best practices

1. **Always return early.** Push long-running work to a background job and return `2xx`
   immediately — a slow endpoint is indistinguishable from a failing one.
2. **Favour idempotent processing.** Deduplicate on the idempotency key so a redelivery is a no-op.
3. **Default to `HTTPS` endpoints.** Only HTTPS URLs are accepted, and certificates are validated.

### ♻️ Delivery semantics

Callbacks are delivered **at least once** and may arrive **out of order**. Deduplicate on the
idempotency key, and reconcile against
`GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions/{transactionId}/status` before overwriting stored state.

`2xx` marks the event delivered (`202` with an empty body is recommended), `4xx` is a permanent

post.description:
Perform a cash in: a customer hands cash to a retailer, and the retailer transfers the equivalent electronic money from their wallet to the customer's wallet.

Set `reference` to your own idempotency/reconciliation key. If the response status is `PENDING`, poll `GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions/{transactionId}/status` — a final status is available within 24 hours at the latest.

200.description: The cash in was processed. Check `status` — a `PENDING` result must be polled via the transaction status endpoint.

get.description:
Retrieve the general RSA public key used to encrypt sensitive data such as PIN codes.

The key has no validity period by default, but it can be revoked at any time. A revoked or invalid key produces error code `4003` — fetch a fresh key and retry. Cache the key, but be ready to refetch on `4003`.

post.description:
Generate a secure Orange Money QR code (and the matching deep links) for a merchant payment.

The payment itself is **asynchronous**: once the customer completes it, a callback is `POST`ed to `X-Callback-Url` — or, if that header is omitted, to the URL registered for the merchant via `POST /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback`. See the **Callbacks** chapter for headers, signature verification and retry semantics.

Operation-specific business errors are returned. An expired QR code yields error code `4004`.

Sent to your `X-Callback-Url` (or to the merchant callback registered via `POST /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback`) once the customer's payment reaches a final state.

`reference` echoes your own reference and `transactionId` is the Orange Money identifier — either can be used to reconcile. Only act on `status: SUCCESS`.

MerchantCallBack.title: MerchantCallBack
MerchantCallBack.description: A callback endpoint registered against a merchant or retailer code.

callbackUrl.description:
HTTPS URL that will receive payment notifications.

Callback endpoints are exposed to the internet, so for safety only `HTTPS` URLs are accepted and the TLS certificate is validated — self-signed, expired or hostname-mismatched certificates cause delivery to fail.

apiKey.description:
Shared secret used to authenticate the callback. We send it back to you verbatim in the `Authorization: Basic {apiKey}` header of every callback.

Write-only: it is never returned by `GET /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback`. Compare it in constant time, and still verify `X-Sonatel-Signature`.

CallbackAcceptEncoding.name: Accept-Encoding
CallbackAcceptEncoding.description: Content encodings accepted by the delivery agent. A compressed response body is supported, but an empty body is preferred.

CallbackUserAgent.name: User-Agent
CallbackUserAgent.description:
Identifies the Orange Money callback delivery agent.

⚠️ **Never** use this header for authentication — it is trivially spoofed. Authenticate with `X-Sonatel-Signature`.

CallbackIdempotencyKey.name: X-Sonatel-Idempotency-Key
CallbackIdempotencyKey.description:
Unique identifier of the **event**, stable across every retry of that event.

Persist it with a unique constraint and short-circuit any key you have already processed: callbacks are delivered *at least once*, so without this check a redelivery will double-apply the transaction.

CallbackSignature.name: X-Sonatel-Signature
CallbackSignature.description:
HMAC signature of the raw request body, computed with your **partner endpoint secret**.

| Version | Hash | Encoding |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `v1` | `SHA256` | `hex` |

The value is a comma-separated list of `key=value` pairs:

- `t`  — Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the signature was generated.
- `v1` — lowercase hex `HMAC-SHA256` digest of `"{t},{raw_body}"`, keyed with your endpoint secret. Several `v1=` entries may be present during a secret rotation; accept the request if **any** of them matches.

Verify by (1) reading the **raw** body before parsing, (2) rejecting a `t` outside your tolerance window (300 s is a sensible default) to block replays, and (3) comparing digests in constant time. See the *Callbacks* chapter of the API description for ready-made Node.js, Python and PHP snippets.

XCallbackUrlRequired.name: X-Callback-Url
XCallbackUrlRequired.description: HTTPS URL that will receive the callback once the operation completes. Must be publicly reachable. Plain HTTP is rejected and TLS certificates are validated.

XCallbackUrlOptional.name: X-Callback-Url
XCallbackUrlOptional.description: HTTPS URL that will receive the payment notification. If omitted, the callback registered for the merchant via `POST /api/notification/v1/merchantcallback` is used instead. Plain HTTP is rejected and TLS certificates are validated.

XApiKey.name: X-Api-Key
XApiKey.description: Optional merchant API key, when your contract provisions one.

BadRequest.description:
Bad request — the payload or parameters failed validation.

Supported error codes:
- `20` — Invalid input parameter value
- `21` — Missing body
- `22` — Invalid body
- `23` — Missing body field
- `24` — Invalid body field
- `25` — Missing header
- `26` — Invalid header value
- `27` — Missing query-string parameter
- `28` — Invalid query-string parameter value

Business errors (`2xxx`, `4xxx`) are also returned with this status — see the **Error codes** table in the API description.

Unauthorized.description:
Unauthorized — the access token is missing, malformed or expired.

Supported error codes:
- `10` — Full authentication is required to access this resource

Forbidden.description:
Forbidden — the token is valid but your application is not allowed to call this operation.

Supported error codes:
- `11` — Access forbidden

NotFound.description:
Not found — the requested resource does not exist.

Supported error codes:
- `60` — Resource not found

MethodNotAllowed.description:
Method not allowed for this resource.

Supported error codes:
- `61` — Bad method used

TooManyRequests.description:
Too many requests — the rate limit was exceeded (sandbox: 60 requests/minute). Back off and retry.

Supported error codes:
- `9` — Too Many Requests

InternalServerError.description:
Internal server error.

Supported error codes:
- `50` — Internal server error
- `51` — Due to some technical problems, your request is in a pending state — poll `GET /api/eWallet/v1/transactions/{transactionId}/status` for the final outcome
- `1` — Your request cannot be processed at this time, please try again later
